sections.h2: What the Franklin County recorder handles
sections.html:
Every deed that hands a Franklin County house to a new owner ends up at the Recorder of Deeds, along with the deed of trust that secures the buyer's loan and the release that follows a payoff. Once the office accepts a paper, it joins the public land record. Union is the county seat, and the county's home page puts a Record My Deeds link next to the tax payment and marriage license links.

The assessor depends on this record. Its staff processes more than 10,000 instruments and deeds a year from the county GIS department to keep parcel and ownership data current, and over 6,300 subdivisions are on file. When a deed is never recorded, that data keeps showing the previous owner.

Phone the office before you go to learn its room, hours and the payment types it takes. Ask also whether your title company is allowed to file for you.

sections.h2: Why recording matters when you sell
sections.html:
The county's population is about 108,090, and builders took out 794 permits in 2025, so new construction competes with resale. Monthly owner costs run $1,442 with a mortgage and $505 without, and median rent is $893.

A recorded deed is what a buyer's lender looks for as proof of ownership. It also steers the assessor's mail. RSMo 137.180 requires an increased value to be reported to the record owner, so a deed that is not on file can send a buyer's notice to the seller's old address.

Missouri's recording statute, RSMo 59.310, gives a recorder the right to bounce a paper that ignores the layout rules. The county may still record such a paper for an extra $25. A title company will usually check these points, but you can too:

  • One-sided pages, not permanently bound and not on a continuous form
  • Black or dark ink, with letters no smaller than eight points and clean enough to copy
  • Light paper, 20-pound or heavier, free of watermarks
  • Dark-ink signatures with the name typed, printed or stamped underneath
  • A three-inch blank band at the top of page one, kept clear for the Recorder's certification, and three-quarters of an inch of margin elsewhere

Exempt from these layout rules: papers signed before 2002, military separation papers, anything signed abroad, certified copies and court judgments. If the office turns your paper away, it goes back to whoever presented it, with the reason.

Below that blank band, the statute asks for the details that identify the transaction. If something cannot fit, page one should say where it can be found in the document.

  • The title of the paper and its date
  • All grantors and their marital status, plus all grantees
  • Statutory addresses, if any
  • The legal description
  • Book and page references wherever a statute requires them

Legal descriptions get copied wrong more than anything else. Lift yours from the vesting deed or title commitment, not the tax bill, and let the title company proofread it before signing. A slip can force a corrective deed and a second set of fees.

RSMo 59.310 caps what a recorder can charge. The amounts below are the statute's base figures, so confirm the total for your page count with the Franklin County office before mailing a check.

Base recorder fees in RSMo 59.310
ServiceFee
Deed or other instrument$5 first page, $3 each added page
Extra items in a release or assignment$5 each beyond the first
Nonconforming paper$25 extra
Copy of a recorded instrumentUp to $2 first page, $1 each added page
Subdivision plat or survey$25 per sheet

sections.h2: What to bring to the counter
sections.html:
Walk in with the signed deed already checked against the page rules, a payment sized to the page count and, if the deed involves a loan payoff, the release that goes with it. Bring the legal description in a form you can compare, because staff cannot fix a description for you. A release or assignment that covers several items is charged per item beyond the first, so count them before you pay.

If anything is wrong, the office hands the paper back with the reason in writing. That costs you a second trip, and it can cost a closing date. A phone call ahead, with the first-page details read aloud, is cheap insurance when the sale is on a deadline.

Plats and surveys are priced by the sheet, and a copy of a recorded paper is charged by the page. If you only need proof of a past transfer, ask for a copy and a certificate instead of filing anything new.

Recording a deed does not touch the tax bill. The Franklin County Collector, Doug Trentmann, works from Room 103 at 400 E Locust in Union and can be reached at 636-583-6353. One statement from that office may cover the county and 64 other taxing entities.

Tax is due by December 31. Afterward it is delinquent, and RSMo 140.100 adds an 18 percent penalty on the year's delinquency. Delinquent land goes up for sale on the fourth Monday in August (RSMo 140.150), and owners can pay right up to the sale.

Buyers get one shortcut. If you purchase fewer than 30 days after the county mailed the statement, you may take an assessment appeal directly to the State Tax Commission. In all other cases the Board of Equalization goes first, and it takes filings through the second Monday in July.

sections.h2: Step by step after you sell
sections.html:
Many sales close at a title company, which can draft the deed, collect the recording fee and file the paper. In a private sale or a family transfer, you handle that yourself:

  1. Have the deed prepared to the layout rules above.
  2. Check the legal description against the vesting deed.
  3. Confirm the page count and the fee with the Recorder's office.
  4. Deliver the deed, then keep the recorded copy as your proof.

Before closing, tell the title company which tax years are open and whether a judgment, mechanic's claim or other lien is on the property. An inherited house or one with tenants may need other papers recorded first, so ask what comes ahead of the deed and what a cash buyer would pay off at the table.

Finish by giving the buyer a clear contact at the Collector and the Assessor, so the first tax bill and any value notice reach the new owner and not you. Hold on to your closing statement and the recorded deed together in one folder, since later questions about who owed what usually trace back to those two papers.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Franklin County?
faqs.a: With the county Recorder of Deeds. The county home page has a Record My Deeds link. Call for the room, hours and payment methods, or ask your title company to file.

faqs.q: How much is the recording fee in Franklin County?
faqs.a: The statute's base amount is $5 for page one and $3 for each page after. The office can quote the total for your page count.

faqs.q: Why did the Recorder reject my deed?
faqs.a: Most often a layout problem. RSMo 59.310 calls for a three-inch top margin, dark ink, type of at least eight points and the first-page details. The paper comes back with a written reason, or it can be recorded for an extra $25.

faqs.q: Does recording pay off property taxes?
faqs.a: No. Taxes are owed to the Collector at 636-583-6353 by December 31. Unpaid land can be offered at the August sale.

faqs.q: What area does the Franklin County Recorder serve?
faqs.a: The whole county, including Union, Washington, Pacific, Sullivan, New Haven, St. Clair, Berger and Gerald, plus unincorporated places such as Gray Summit and Villa Ridge.
